notes.summary: Time and Work covers rates of working, combined work, efficiency, man-days, wages and pipes and cisterns. SSC CGL asks 1-3 questions on it in Tier-I and Tier-II, and most of them can be solved in under a minute with the LCM (total work units) method.
keyPoints: If A finishes a job in n days, A does 1/n of it per day. A and B together take (a × b)/(a + b) days: 20 and 30 days together take 600/50 = 12 days.
LCM method: take total work = LCM of the given days so that every daily output is a whole number. A = 15 days, B = 20 days → work = 60 units, A = 4 units/day, B = 3 units/day.
Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If A is 50% more efficient than B (efficiency 3 : 2), A takes 2/3 of B's time (time 2 : 3).
Chain rule: M1 × D1 × H1 / W1 = M2 × D2 × H2 / W2. 8 men × 15 days × 6 h = 720 man-hours, so 10 men working 8 h a day need 720 ÷ 80 = 9 days.
Wages are shared in the ratio of work done, not days taken. If C does 1/8 of the job, C gets 1/8 of the total payment.
Pair rates: if (A+B), (B+C) and (C+A) are given, add them to get 2(A+B+C), then halve. 12, 15, 20 days → 5 + 4 + 3 = 12 units = 2(A+B+C), so all three do 6 units/day.
Pipes: a filling pipe is positive work, an emptying pipe or leak is negative work. Fill in 10 h, empty in 15 h → net 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so the tank fills in 30 h.
Leak shortcut: if a pipe fills a tank in x h alone and in y h with a leak, the leak empties the full tank in xy/(y − x) h. 6 h and 8 h → 48/2 = 24 h.
Alternate-day work: find the work done in one full cycle, count the full cycles, then finish the leftover units with whoever works next.
traps: Adding days instead of rates: 10 days and 15 days together is NOT 25 days; it is 6 days.
Splitting wages in the ratio of days taken instead of the ratio of work done (efficiency).
In alternate-day questions, forgetting to check whose turn it is on the last, fractional day.
Treating a leak or an emptying pipe as positive work.
When workers leave or join midway, forgetting to subtract the work already finished before recalculating.
notes.examTip: Convert every question to total work units using the LCM of the given days right away; it removes fractions and saves 20-30 seconds per question.

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 20 days and B can do it in 30 days. In how many days will they finish it working together?
questions.explanation:
Take total work = LCM(20, 30) = 60 units.
A does 60/20 = 3 units/day and B does 60/30 = 2 units/day.
Together they do 5 units/day.
Time = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days. (Shortcut: 20 × 30/(20 + 30) = 600/50 = 12 days.)

questions.text: 12 men can complete a work in 18 days. How many men are needed to complete the same work in 8 days?
questions.explanation:
Total work = 12 × 18 = 216 man-days.
Men needed to finish it in 8 days = 216 ÷ 8 = 27 men.

questions.text: A and B together can do a work in 8 days. A alone can do it in 12 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
questions.explanation:
B's one-day work = 1/8 − 1/12 = (3 − 2)/24 = 1/24.
So B alone takes 24 days.
Shortcut: 8 × 12/(12 − 8) = 96/4 = 24 days.

questions.text: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours and pipe B can empty the full tank in 15 hours. If both pipes are opened together on an empty tank, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation:
Take the tank = LCM(10, 15) = 30 units.
Pipe A adds 3 units/hour and pipe B removes 2 units/hour.
Net filling = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/hour.
Time to fill = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 hours.

questions.text: A is 50% more efficient than B. If B alone can finish a work in 30 days, in how many days can A alone finish it?
questions.explanation:
50% more efficient means efficiency A : B = 150 : 100 = 3 : 2.
Time is inversely proportional to efficiency, so time A : B = 2 : 3.
B takes 30 days, so 3 parts = 30 and 1 part = 10.
A takes 2 × 10 = 20 days.

questions.text: 8 men working 6 hours a day can finish a work in 15 days. In how many days will 10 men finish the same work working 8 hours a day?
A can do a piece of work in 15 days and B can do it in 20 days. They work together for 4 days and then A leaves. In how many days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Total work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units; A = 4 units/day, B = 3 units/day.
In 4 days together they do 4 × 7 = 28 units.
Remaining work = 60 − 28 = 32 units.
B alone needs 32 ÷ 3 = 10 2/3 days.

questions.text: A, B and C can complete a work in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. In how many days will they complete it working together?
questions.explanation:
Total work = LCM(10, 12, 15) = 60 units.
A = 6, B = 5 and C = 4 units/day, so together = 15 units/day.
Time = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.

questions.text: A and B together can do a work in 12 days, B and C together in 15 days, and C and A together in 20 days. In how many days can A, B and C together finish the work?
questions.explanation:
Total work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units.
(A+B) = 5, (B+C) = 4 and (C+A) = 3 units/day.
Adding: 2(A+B+C) = 12, so A+B+C = 6 units/day.
Time = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days. (Forgetting to halve gives the wrong answer 5 days.)

questions.text: A can do a work in 6 days and B in 8 days. With the help of C, they finish the work in 3 days and are paid ₹4800 in all. What is C's share?
questions.explanation:
In 3 days, A does 3/6 = 1/2 of the work and B does 3/8 of it.
C's work = 1 − 1/2 − 3/8 = 1/8.
Wages are shared in the ratio of work done.
C's share = 1/8 × 4800 = ₹600.

questions.text: 2 men and 3 women can finish a work in 10 days, while 3 men and 4 women can finish it in 7 days. In how many days will 1 man alone finish the work?
questions.explanation:
10(2M + 3W) = 7(3M + 4W)
20M + 30W = 21M + 28W, so M = 2W (one man works like two women).
Take 1 woman = 1 unit/day and 1 man = 2 units/day.
Total work = 10 × (2 × 2 + 3 × 1) = 70 units.
1 man alone takes 70 ÷ 2 = 35 days.

questions.text: A takes 10 days less than B to complete a work. Working together, they complete it in 12 days. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.explanation:
Let B take x days; then A takes (x − 10) days.
1/x + 1/(x − 10) = 1/12.
Try x = 30: A takes 20 days, and 1/30 + 1/20 = 2/60 + 3/60 = 5/60 = 1/12, which matches.
So B alone takes 30 days (A takes 20 days).

questions.text: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 15 minutes respectively, while pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 minutes. If all three pipes are opened together on an empty tank, in how much time will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation:
Take the tank = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units.
A fills 5, B fills 4 and C empties 3 units per minute.
Net filling = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units per minute.
Time = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 minutes.

questions.text: A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it takes 8 hours to fill the tank. In how many hours can the leak alone empty the full tank?
questions.explanation:
Leak's rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = (4 − 3)/24 = 1/24 of the tank per hour.
So the leak empties the full tank in 24 hours.
Shortcut: xy/(y − x) = 6 × 8/(8 − 6) = 48/2 = 24 hours.

questions.text: 40 men can finish a work in 30 days. They work for 10 days, and then 10 more men join them. In how many more days will the remaining work be finished?
questions.explanation:
Total work = 40 × 30 = 1200 man-days.
Work done in the first 10 days = 40 × 10 = 400 man-days.
Remaining work = 800 man-days, now done by 40 + 10 = 50 men.
Days needed = 800 ÷ 50 = 16 more days.

questions.text: 3 men or 5 women can do a work in 12 days. How many days will 6 men and 5 women take to do the same work?
questions.explanation:
3 men = 5 women, so 5 women can be replaced by 3 men.
6 men + 5 women = 6 + 3 = 9 men.
Work = 3 × 12 = 36 man-days.
Time for 9 men = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 days.

questions.text: A can do a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work on alternate days, with A working on the first day. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation:
Total work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units; A = 3 units/day, B = 2 units/day.
One 2-day cycle (A then B) = 5 units.
7 cycles = 14 days = 35 units, leaving 1 unit.
Day 15 is A's turn: 1 unit at 3 units/day takes 1/3 day.
Total = 14 1/3 days.

questions.text: A and B together can finish a work in 30 days. They work together for 20 days, after which B leaves. A finishes the remaining work in 20 more days. In how many days can A alone finish the whole work?
questions.explanation:
In 20 days together they finish 20/30 = 2/3 of the work.
The remaining 1/3 is done by A alone in 20 days.
So A alone does the whole work in 20 × 3 = 60 days.

questions.text: 12 men working 8 hours a day can dig a trench 120 m long in 10 days. How many men, working 6 hours a day, are needed to dig a trench 90 m long in 12 days?
A can do 80% of a work in 20 days. He then calls B, and together they finish the remaining work in 3 days. How long would B alone take to do the whole work?
questions.explanation:
A does 80% in 20 days, so A alone needs 20 ÷ 0.8 = 25 days for the whole work.
The remaining 20% is done by A and B together in 3 days, so together they need 3 ÷ 0.2 = 15 days.
B's one-day work = 1/15 − 1/25 = (5 − 3)/75 = 2/75.
B alone takes 75/2 = 37 1/2 days.
